Secondary Schools Football Championship: Waiqele College beat Labasa College 1-0 to book semi-final spot

item.content:encoded:
Waiqele College have secured their place in the semi-finals of the 2026 Extra Fiji Secondary Schools Football Championship Open Grade Girls competition after beating Labasa College 1-0 in the quarter-finals.

Team Manager Anjini Chand says she is proud of the girls' achievement and has expressed her gratitude to God Almighty, the team's sponsors, parents, school management and teachers for their support in helping the team reach the semi-finals..

Chand says the girls gave their best in the quarter-final and she is confident they can reach the final and retain the trophy in Labasa.

Tavua College also advanced to the semi-finals after beating Nukuloa College 2-1, while Dreketi Central defeated Suva Muslim College 1-0 and Lekutu Secondary School beat Pandit Vishnu Deo Memorial College 2-0.

The semi-finals are scheduled to be played later today between 2pm and 3.30pm.

item.title: No disqualification as Grammar and Lelean set for Super Deans Final
item.description: Navitalai Naivalurua · 20/08/2026 Suva Grammar School and Lelean Memorial School will feature in the Vodafone Fiji Secondary Schools Rugby Union Super Deans Final, with no teams disqualified from the competition.
item.content:encoded:
Navitalai Naivalurua · 20/08/2026

Suva Grammar School and Lelean Memorial School will feature in the Vodafone Fiji Secondary Schools Rugby Union Super Deans Final, with no teams disqualified from the competition.

This is after false information is being widely shared on social media claiming that the Lelean Memorial School Under-18 rugby side has been disqualified and Nasinu Secondary School have taken their place.

fijivillage News received confirmation today from Fiji Secondary Schools Rugby Union Vice President Development Biu Colati, who says they have not received any complaints against Lelean Memorial School.

Grammar will face Lelean at 6.10pm at the HFC Bank Stadium on Saturday.

item.title: MGM U17 girls battle hard for win over Vunimono
item.description: MGM High School’s Under-17 girls netball team secured a hard-fought 22-11 victory over Vunimono High School in their Crest Chicken Secondary School Netball Competition pool match . The Vunimono side from Nausori remained competitive throughout the game, but MGM stayed composed under pressure and maintained their momentum to claim the win.
item.content:encoded:
MGM High School’s Under-17 girls netball team secured a hard-fought 22-11 victory over Vunimono High School in their Crest Chicken Secondary School Netball Competition pool match .

The Vunimono side from Nausori remained competitive throughout the game, but MGM stayed composed under pressure and maintained their momentum to claim the win.

MGM captain Adi Sera Faith Dawai says the result reflects the team’s hard work and dedication during their preparation.

She says the team has been training since the beginning of the year, with regular morning and afternoon sessions helping them prepare for the competition.

Dawai says the journey has not been easy, with players putting in extra effort through early morning training sessions before school.

She thanked their parents, teachers, managers and sponsor Ditesh Patel for their continued support.

Dawai says Patel has been a strong supporter of the school’s sporting teams, including athletics and netball .

She says the competition has been challenging, with every team giving their best effort on court.

Dawai adds the team will continue working hard as they aim to achieve their goals in the competition.

In other pool results, Nadroga Arya College lost to Jasper Williams High School 15-9 in the Under-15 girls grade, while Levuka Public School defeated Saint Joseph Secondary School 20-10 in the Under-19 girls competition.

In the open girls grade, Koro Island High School defeated Yat Sen Secondary School 15-13, while Central College Lautoka and Saint Francis College played out an 11-all draw.

In the open boys grade, Ra High School defeated Noco Secondary School 19-6, while Bhawani Dayal Secondary School secured a 13-11 win over Central College.

Due to wet weather conditions the quarter-finals have been moved to tomorrow.

item.title: Former Fiji Bati captain Tui Kamikamica retires on medical grounds
item.description: Former Vodafone Fiji Bati captain and long-serving Melbourne Storm prop Tui Kamikamica has announced his immediate retirement from rugby league on medical grounds. Kamikamica has captained the Bati since 2023 and represented Fiji in 23 Test matches.
item.content:encoded:
Former Vodafone Fiji Bati captain and long-serving Melbourne Storm prop Tui Kamikamica has announced his immediate retirement from rugby league on medical grounds.

Kamikamica has captained the Bati since 2023 and represented Fiji in 23 Test matches.

The powerful forward has made 142 NRL appearances for the Melbourne Storm and has been part of the club’s leadership group since 2025.

Earlier this week, Kamikamica was honoured as a Life Member of Melbourne Storm, becoming the first Pacific Islander and first Fijian to receive the prestigious recognition.

This year also marked his 10th year with the Melbourne-based club.

Kamikamica leaves the game after a decade with the Storm, having established himself as one of Fiji’s leading players on the international stage.

item.title: Ratu Finau girls overcome challenges to reach national netball competition
item.description: Temalesi Vono , Antornette Vuniuca · 20/08/2026 Ratu Finau Secondary School netball coach and teacher Iliesa Rasolo says his players have shown significant improvement after qualifying for the Crest Chicken Secondary School Netball Finals.
item.content:encoded:
Temalesi Vono , Antornette Vuniuca · 20/08/2026

Ratu Finau Secondary School netball coach and teacher Iliesa Rasolo says his players have shown significant improvement after qualifying for the Crest Chicken Secondary School Netball Finals.

Ratu Finau Secondary School travelled from Lakeba Island to Suva to compete in the Under-15 and Under-17 grades.

Rasolo says the team began preparing early and is determined to make the most of the opportunity after a tough qualifying campaign.

He says reaching the nationals is a major achievement for the school , particularly after competing against some of the stronger schools during the mid-term competition.

However, playing in front of a large crowd and travelling to Suva presented new challenges for the young players.

Rasolo says the girls were nervous at first, particularly because it was their first experience playing in front of such a large crowd and against unfamiliar teams.

He says fundraising for the trip was another challenge, with parents taking the lead in making the team's participation possible.

Rasolo is encouraging more schools, particularly those from rural and remote areas, to take part in the national competition.

The Crest Chicken Secondary School Netball Competition continues today, with the finals to be played tomorrow.
